beats.intro: Chapter six, lesson three. The endoplasmic reticulum and the Golgi apparatus. [[liver]]After a meal, or a medicine, your liver cells go to work. They break down poisons, and they build the fats and proteins your blood needs. [[cell]]Here is the whole cell map from our tour. [[lit]]Two parts are lit up today. The endoplasmic reticulum, called the {{ER|E R}}, and the Golgi apparatus. [[ask]]How do they turn raw materials into finished products?
beats.system: These two belong to a larger team. [[six]]The endomembrane system has six components. The nuclear envelope, the {{ER|E R}}, the Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, vacuoles, and the plasma membrane. [[link]]They are either continuous with each other, or linked when vesicles carry material between them. Lysosomes and vacuoles wait for the next lesson. [[er]]The {{ER|E R}} is the biggest of them. In most eukaryotic cells, it makes up more than half of all the membrane. [[env]]And it is continuous with the nuclear envelope, so the space inside the {{ER|E R}} opens straight onto the nucleus.
beats.regions: The {{ER|E R}} is a network of flattened sacs and tubes. [[lumen]]Each sac is called a cisterna, and the plural is cisternae. The space inside is the {{ER|E R}} lumen. [[smooth]]It has two main regions. Smooth {{ER|E R}} has no ribosomes at all. [[rough]]Rough {{ER|E R}} has ribosomes attached to the outside of its membrane. Those are called bound ribosomes. [[trans]]And where the {{ER|E R}} passes work along, a piece of its membrane buds off as a transport vesicle. This part is called transitional {{ER|E R}}.
beats.q1: Quick check. Which part is smooth {{ER|E R}}?
beats.smooth: Start with smooth {{ER|E R}}, and back in the liver cell. [[lipid]]First, it synthesizes lipids, the fats and oils the cell needs for its membranes. [[carb]]Second, it helps metabolize carbohydrates. [[poison]]Third, it detoxifies poisons. A liver cell packed with smooth {{ER|E R}} can make drugs and alcohol less harmful. [[calcium]]And fourth, it stores calcium ions, which the cell can release when it needs a signal. [[none]]No ribosomes are needed for any of this work.
beats.rough: Now the rough {{ER|E R}}. [[bound]]Its bound ribosomes build proteins, and the new chain is threaded into the lumen. [[sugar]]There, sugars are attached. A protein with carbohydrate bonded to it is called a glycoprotein. [[secret]]Many of these are made for secretion, so they leave the cell. [[membrane]]Rough {{ER|E R}} also adds to the cell's own membrane, so it is called the membrane factory. [[vesicle]]And it hands its products on in transport vesicles, small bubbles of membrane with cargo inside.
beats.compare: Put the two regions side by side. [[ribo]]Rough has ribosomes, smooth has none. [[shape]]Rough is mostly flat sheets, smooth is mostly tubes. [[job]]Rough makes glycoproteins and membrane. Smooth makes lipids, handles carbohydrates, detoxifies, and stores calcium. [[one]]But they are one connected network, with one lumen.
beats.q2: Quick check. Match each job to its region.
beats.golgi: Next stop, the Golgi apparatus. [[stack]]It is a stack of flattened membranous sacs, again called cisternae. [[cis]]One side is the cis face. It is the receiving side, and it sits near the {{ER|E R}}. [[trans]]The other side is the trans face. It is the shipping side. [[move]]Material moves through the stack, from cis to trans. [[mod]]On the way, the Golgi modifies the products of the {{ER|E R}}. [[make]]It also manufactures certain macromolecules of its own. [[sort]]Finally, it sorts and packages materials into transport vesicles, ready to leave.
beats.example: Let's follow one product all the way. A pancreas cell makes digestive enzymes, and they are glycoproteins. [[ribo]]A bound ribosome on the rough {{ER|E R}} builds the protein chain. [[lumen]]The chain enters the lumen, and a carbohydrate is attached. It is now a glycoprotein. [[bud]]A transport vesicle buds off from the transitional {{ER|E R}}. [[arrive]]The vesicle reaches the cis face of the Golgi, and joins it. [[through]]The product moves through the cisternae, and the Golgi modifies it. [[ship]]At the trans face, it is packaged into a new vesicle. [[leave]]That vesicle carries the finished glycoprotein away, toward the cell surface, or to other parts of the cell. We will follow it further next lesson.
beats.q3: Quick check. Put the journey in order.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]The {{ER|E R}} is continuous with the nuclear envelope, and it is more than half the membrane in most cells. [[w2]]Smooth {{ER|E R}} has no ribosomes. It makes lipids, metabolizes carbohydrates, detoxifies poisons, and stores calcium. [[w3]]Rough {{ER|E R}} has bound ribosomes. It makes glycoproteins for secretion, and builds membrane. [[w4]]The Golgi has a cis face that receives, and a trans face that ships. [[end]]Now try the practice.
beats.final1: Chapter practice. Six questions on the {{ER|E R}} and the Golgi apparatus.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter six, lesson three. Next, lysosomes, vacuoles, and the whole traffic route.
